articles.title: Rangers beat Celtic again to cut Premiership lead to two points

articles.summary: Unbeaten Everton move up to fifth in the Premier League, with Thierno Barry's goal making the difference against 10-man Ipswich Town.

articles.title: Spurs lose again as Villa hold on for first league win
articles.summary: Aston Villa pick up their first win of the Premier League season after five matches, holding off a late push from a Tottenham Hotspur side who remain without a win in the league.

articles.title: Brighton humbling 'a big lesson' for Arsenal - Arteta

articles.title: A Coventry win 25 years in the making
articles.summary: Coventry City's win over Nottingham Forest - thanks to Jay Dasilva's goal - was a victory which was over 25 years in the making following some dark days for the Sky Blues.

articles.title: Clark resigns as Hartlepool boss in post-match interview
articles.summary: Lee Clark resigns as Hartlepool United head coach after a sixth loss in seven games following the 3-1 home defeat by Worthing.

articles.title: No revival in sight for 'fragile' Spurs after Villa defeat
articles.summary: Tottenham look no closer to solving their problems as they slip to a home defeat by Aston Villa to add to their Premier League misery.

articles.title: Moyes demands more from Everton - but don't mention Europe
articles.summary: Fifth in the Premier League table and yet to lose this season, Everton are on the up, but boss David Moyes wants further improvements - and don't mention Europe.

articles.title: Suzuki proves worthy replacement for Martinez at Villa
articles.summary: Aston Villa new boy Zion Suzuki deserves as much credit as anyone for their first Premier League win of the season at struggling Tottenham.

articles.title: Arsenal score last-minute equaliser to deny Man Utd first WSL win
articles.summary: Arsenal steal a last gasp leveller through Smilla Holmberg, denying Eva Olid her first win as Manchester United manager in her third game in charge.

articles.title: 'It's a big lesson to learn' - Arteta on 'painful' Brighton defeat
articles.summary: Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta says Arsenal were "very far" from the standards required to compete after the Gunners lost 3-0 to Brighton - their first defeat in the Premier League this season.
